versions.label: GS 0.999 (this build)
changes: ammo.js is no longer selected by default in the Dependencies tab. It stays in the list and can still be turned on, and scenes that already use it still load it with gsRequire('ammo').

versions.label: GS 0.998
changes: The version picker and Cardboard VR button live in a new Meta Settings tab, so they no longer crowd the top of the window.
All tabs open from a hamburger at the top left of the menu window. The active tab name stays visible next to it; Esc or a click outside closes the list.
A new Render tab takes side-by-side VR180-style screenshots and screen recordings (equirectangular, default 180° field of view, saved to your device).

versions.label: GS 0.997
changes: The Community tab shows each scene as a large tile in a responsive grid (several columns in a wide window, one column on a phone).
When you save a scene, a screenshot thumbnail is taken from the initial camera view and shown on the tile.
Each scene has an editable multiline description. It is left blank if nothing has been written yet, and you can change it.

versions.label: GS 0.996
changes: Technical mode now has a checkbox at the top of the 🛠 Technical tab, which is always in the menu (also in the headset). It replaces the Off/On button in Controls, still asks before turning on, and keeps your earlier choice.
Technical features are hidden until Technical mode is checked, then show with a green outline so you can tell them apart, in the normal window and in VR / AR.
The Technical mode checkbox has a green border, so it is easy to see on the dark menu even when unchecked.

versions.label: GS 0.995
changes: New Technical mode (Controls tab › Technical mode, off by default, remembered in this browser): for advanced setup such as permissions outside normal browser use and developer tools. It asks before turning on and works from the headset menu too.

With Technical mode on, a new 🛠 Technical tab lists advanced items. The first is “Quest passthrough camera (ADB)”: the steps and the adb command (with a Copy button) that let Quest Browser use the passthrough cameras when it only offers the avatar camera and the request fails with “OverconstrainedError”, a Check again button, and the camera details.

The 📷 camera details and help moved into that item. With Technical mode off the camera works as before with whatever cameras are listed, and on a Quest with only the avatar camera it just says: Passthrough camera needs extra setup: turn on Technical mode in Settings.

versions.label: GS 0.994
changes: The 📷 camera preview in the chat window was rebuilt: the camera now plays in one hidden video and GS draws every frame into the preview itself, in the normal window and inside VR / AR (where the old preview could stay blank).

A small status line under the camera picture says which camera is on, its size and whether frames are coming in (for example “camera: Quest passthrough (left) 1280×960 · playing”), or the exact error.

New Details button under the camera picture: shows the browser version, the camera permission, every camera the device lists and the exact error, with a Copy button. It opens on its own when Quest only offers the avatar camera.

Only the avatar camera on Quest 3? The hint and help now point to the switch that fixes it: Quest Settings › Privacy & safety › Browser › Headset cameras (and tick Headset cameras, not just Virtual cameras, when Quest asks).

New for scenes: gsPassthroughTexture() puts the live camera feed (the Quest passthrough camera, or the back / default camera elsewhere) on any object, sharing the chat camera. The AI knows how to use it, and the camera picture is never saved in exports.

versions.label: GS 0.993
changes: The AR / VR toggle is now in the menu inside the headset too, at the top next to Exit VR, and you can click it with the controller ray. It shows the mode you're in and uses the same setting as the desktop toggle.
In VR, picking AR switches straight into AR (passthrough). If the headset doesn't allow the instant switch, a pop-up asks for one more tap to enter AR.
In AR, picking VR covers your room with the colour sky right away, and picking AR shows the room again, without leaving the session.

A soft light now sits just above the menu in VR / AR, so the menu and the space around you are visible in dark, shadowy scenes. It follows the menu, turns off while the menu is hidden, and is never saved or exported with your scene. The menu itself now ignores scene fog, so it always stays readable.

On Meta Quest 3, the chat window's 📷 camera list now includes the passthrough camera, the same view of your room you see in AR, not just the avatar camera. GS asks for the Headset cameras permission, then lists and switches to the passthrough camera; if only the avatar camera shows up, a hint explains how to allow it.

versions.label: GS 0.992
changes: Take photos with your camera: a new 📷 button sits next to the 📎 upload button in the chat window (under More on phones). It opens a live camera preview between the messages and the buttons.
Pick which camera to use (front, back, webcam…) from the list under the preview. Your choice is remembered.
Take photo attaches the picture to your next message, just like an uploaded photo. ✕ closes the camera and turns it off.
If the camera is blocked, missing or busy, a short message in the panel says why and how to fix it.

On Meta Quest 3 the photo comes from the headset's passthrough cameras (left or right), and in VR the live preview shows right on the menu window. Quest asks for the Headset cameras permission the first time.

New AR / VR toggle next to Enter VR at the top of the window and in the 🎨 Environment tab of the menu window: AR shows your real room around the scene (passthrough), VR shows the scene with a colour sky. Options your device doesn't support are greyed out, and your choice is remembered.
Inside an AR session, the Environment tab switches between your room and the colour sky right away.

versions.label: GS 0.991
changes: Embed export: the Share tab has an Embed button that gives you an <iframe> code to put your scene on any website. Pick a size (responsive, 800×450, 1280×720 or square) and whether to include Enter VR, see a preview, and copy it. A scene that isn't uploaded yet is uploaded once for you.
Community scenes have an Embed button too, for scenes whose creator allows exports.
The embedded scene is view-only: drag to orbit, Enter VR on headsets that support it, and a small "Made with GS For Anything" link back to the scene.

When you upload to Community you can choose to allow or not allow others to export your scene (on by default; scenes uploaded before this count as allowed). You can change it later on your own scenes with Allow exports / Block exports.

On a scene whose creator turned exports off, other people can't export models or .vrscene files, save it to their device, re-upload it, merge it or embed it. They see a short message instead, and other sites can't embed or frame it. The scene can still be viewed, and its code can still be read in the editor.

versions.label: GS 0.990
changes: Exit VR: in VR, a big red Exit VR button sits at the top of the menu on every tab. Point and click (or pinch) once to leave VR and get the normal 2D page back.
Enter VR and the GS version button now sit side by side at the top of the window, in the chat window's header, instead of at the bottom of the page. The version button still opens the version picker.
On phones the top bar has large tap targets; on narrow windows the labels go compact. VR NOT SUPPORTED is hidden when Cardboard VR is offered.

The Code window scrolls in VR: push the thumbstick up / down while pointing at it (the player doesn't move while you scroll a window), or trigger-drag / pinch-drag it. The code highlighting follows and a scrollbar is drawn. The chat log and other scrolling boxes scroll the same way.

Origin gizmo in VR (Env tab): point at it and hold grip on either controller, then turn your hand; the gizmo and the scene's default orientation rotate with the controller. Let go of grip to stop. Grip elsewhere still switches locomotion.

versions.label: GS 0.989
changes: The 🎤 mic button now says what it is doing, right under the button (and in the VR menu and the VR HUD): downloading the speech model with a percentage (first time only), Listening, Transcribing, Sent, or why it can't listen.
Listening only starts once the speech model is ready, and the model starts loading as soon as you first turn the mic on. Speech recognition runs in the background so the scene stays smooth.
If the microphone is blocked or missing you see it, with how to fix it: on Quest, Settings › Apps › Browser › Microphone / site permissions.
Enter VR asks for the microphone first if you've used the mic before, so the permission question doesn't appear inside the headset. People who never use the mic aren't asked.
Background noise no longer keeps the mic recording forever: it adjusts to the room and a single recording is cut at 15 seconds.
Noise-only results like [Music], [BEEP] or empty text are no longer sent to the chat.
Push-to-talk (A / X on the controller) shows a message when the microphone isn't allowed instead of silently doing nothing.

versions.label: GS 0.988
changes: GS's own pop-ups replace the browser's alert / confirm / prompt boxes: Clear scene, Files → Clear all, the Community theme name and Chat → Prompt → Reset now ask with an in-app pop-up.

In VR the pop-up opens inside the headset view, in front of where you are looking, and you answer it with the controller ray; the menu behind it waits until you answer. Text questions bring up the VR keyboard right under the pop-up.
On desktop and phones the same pop-up shows as a centred window: Escape cancels, Enter confirms, destructive actions focus Cancel first, and buttons are large enough to tap.
Scene code that calls alert / confirm / prompt gets the in-app pop-up too, and the scene AI is told to use gsAlert / gsConfirm / gsPrompt.
Still the browser's own: the file pickers for uploads and imports (the system file chooser can't be replaced).

versions.label: GS 0.987
changes: One active scene at a time: loading a scene from Community, a share link, a scene file, Load Saved or a merge now replaces the scene in the world instead of layering it on top, and the old objects and textures are cleaned up.

Chat history belongs to the active scene: opening another scene shows only that scene's chat history, never the previous scene's stacked alongside it, and new chat replies only continue the active scene.

The Scenes tab shows the current scene; the scene layering controls (Clear first / Layer, per-scene checkboxes and remove buttons, Import Folder, Export Combined) are gone. All export options still work on the active scene: Export / Save to Device, GLB, glTF, FBX, OBJ, Blender, Share link and Upload to Community.
Clear scene starts a fresh blank scene and also clears its chat history.

versions.label: GS 0.986
changes: HDRI and sky domes always fit the whole scene: a dome grows to enclose every object (with room to spare) and refits by itself when objects are added, moved or removed, so big scenes no longer poke through or get cut off by a fixed-size dome. Grounded skyboxes keep their floor in place.
Render distance always reaches everything in the scene, on desktop, phone and in VR, so far-away objects are never clipped. Fog is also pushed out so it no longer hides objects completely.

The scene AI is told to do the same: tag domes, size them from the full scene bounds, set the far plane past everything and call gsFitScene() after building a scene. This also applies with a custom Chat Prompt.

versions.label: GS 0.985
changes: Community uploads and share links now keep the Environment HDRI (a link or a file from your computer) and its Use as background setting, and restore them when the scene loads. Scenes uploaded before this load as before and keep your own HDRI.

Use as background works right away: when a scene loads with an HDRI, the HDRI shows as the background immediately, even if the scene sets its own background colour, so you no longer need to click the checkbox twice.

A scene's HDRI doesn't replace your own saved HDRI: the next scene without one goes back to yours. If storing an HDRI file fails (very large files on vrclaudeinterface.vercel.app), the scene still uploads and opens with the default environment.

versions.label: GS 0.984
changes: Phones and tablets: drag the GS window around by its header with a finger, the same as with a mouse on desktop. Only the header moves the window, so the chat, tabs and fields still scroll normally, and on touch screens the header is at least 44px tall.
The window can't be dragged off screen: on phones it stays inside the visible area above the on-screen keyboard and safe areas.
After a reload the window always opens in its default spot, even if you dragged or resized it. Only its size is remembered, and there is no double-tap reset.

versions.label: GS 0.983
changes: Chat: the Scene and Theme chat input fields are now multi-line, so you can see long messages instead of one scrolling line. They start one line tall, grow a line at a time as you type and wrap long text, and scroll after 7 lines (6 on phones) while keeping the chat history in view.
Chat keys: on desktop Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a new line. On phones Enter adds a new line and the Send button sends, and the keyboard stays up after sending.
VR: the taller chat field is drawn wrapped line by line in the VR menu, with the typing ring around it, and the VR keyboard's Enter key still sends.

versions.label: GS 0.982
changes: Environment → Origin rotation (under Camera): turn the scene's origin so the scene lines up with the view you want, using a 2D gizmo of the X/Y/Z axes as seen from the camera. Drag the ball to rotate, drag the outer ring to roll, click or tap an axis end to point that axis straight at you, or type Yaw/Pitch/Roll. Shift or the Snap 15° toggle snaps, and Reset origin undoes it.
The origin rotation is saved in this browser and with the scene, so Save, scene files, Community uploads and share links keep it. Older scenes open unrotated.
The player, the menus and the lights are not rotated. Physics gravity turns with the scene, GLB/glTF/FBX/OBJ exports bake the rotation in, and the AI is told about the rotation only while one is set.
Works with mouse, touch (44px tap targets on phones) and in VR: the gizmo is painted into the VR menu window and the controller ray can drag it.

versions.label: GS 0.981
changes: VR: every window (the menu, the keyboard and the Hide/Show UI button) is now drawn one way, by painting the real page UI with the HTML canvas renderer. The old hand-drawn VR panels (chat, input bar, side panel, Scenes panel, keyboard, status badge) are gone, and the VR menu is the full menu with all its tabs.

VR: all windows share the same size scale, frame, Fixed/Follow anchoring and controller behaviour: an amber ring shows what the ray points at, trigger clicks, trigger-drag or the thumbstick (with locomotion off) scrolls, and pointing at a text field opens the in-scene keyboard with a cyan typing ring.

VR: better contrast. Text, tab labels, buttons, borders, the selected-tab outline and placeholders now meet WCAG AA in the headset (0 of 39 measured pairs fail, down from 19 of 34), and a renderer bug that drew some labels black on dark backgrounds is fixed.
VR: the Lay down / Sit up option is removed from the VR menu. A saved lay-down setting is cleared and the view starts upright.
VR: Chat → Prompt now works in the headset like on desktop: you can edit the prompt with the VR keyboard and Save it, and Reset asks for a second press instead of a pop-up.

versions.label: GS 0.980
changes: Chat has a new Prompt tab next to Scene and Theme. It shows the full default Scene chat prompt, and you can edit it, Save it, Discard unsaved edits or Reset to default. Your edit is kept in this browser and used for Scene chat and community merges; a "Custom prompt active" badge shows while it is on.

A short required technical section (vr-exec blocks, scene globals, floor and facing) is always added after a custom prompt so scene code keeps running. Custom prompts can be up to 40,000 characters. The auto-fix and theme prompts are shown read-only, and in VR the prompt is read-only.

The default prompt has a new photorealistic lighting and materials section: one motivated shadow-casting key light instead of flat, even lighting, weak fill and ambient, RoomEnvironment reflections, ACES tone mapping, physically based intensities and PBR material values, correct colour spaces, and VR performance limits.
GS's built-in lights are named gsDefaultAmbient and gsDefaultKey so scene code can dim or replace them.

versions.label: GS 0.979
changes: The browser tab now reads "GS For Anything" instead of "Claude VR Chat".
Shared scene pages (/e/ and /s/ links) title the tab with the scene name followed by "GS For Anything".
The GitHub repo is renamed to koshkakochka/gsforanything (https://github.com/koshkakochka/gsforanything). Old krossruiz/gs links redirect.

versions.label: GS 0.978
changes: Phones: while you type in the chat box or the code editor, the panel fills the space above the on-screen keyboard, so the text you are typing, the Send button and the newest messages stay in view. The header, tabs, bottom dock, Hide UI and joysticks step aside while the keyboard is up and come back when it closes. Send keeps the keyboard open.
Phones: less crowded controls. Buttons, tabs, menus and checkboxes are at least 44px tall, text boxes use a 16px font so iOS no longer zooms in, and the screen edges and notch are respected.
Phones: the tabs sit in one row you can scroll sideways, and the chat tools moved behind a "+" button next to the chat box.
Phones in landscape: the chat is a full-height column on the left and the bottom dock moves to the right.
Fixed the on-screen joysticks overlapping the bottom dock on phones.
Desktop, tablet and VR layouts are unchanged.

versions.label: GS 0.977
changes: The desktop camera now uses the standard three.js camera controls, picked in the Controls tab: Orbit (the default, rotating around the scene's center at 0,0,0), Map, Trackball, Fly (drag to look) and First person (click the scene to look around with the mouse, Esc to release, WASD or arrows to walk), plus Off. Each mode lists its keys in the Controls tab.
Removed the custom Orbit and Free-roam controls. A saved Orbit choice stays Orbit, Free-roam becomes First person, and Off stays Off.

Keys move the camera unless you are typing in a text field, even after clicking buttons or panels. The on-screen joysticks appear in Fly and First person, and a game controller drives Orbit, Map, Fly and First person.

versions.label: GS 0.976
changes: Orbit now always rotates around the scene's center (0,0,0): on first load, after Clear scene, after loading a scene, and after Reset Camera View or the gamepad View button. Walking with WASD or the left stick in Orbit used to make the camera circle one point while facing another; now it turns around the point it's looking at.

Free-roam has two small on-screen joysticks in the bottom corners. They are thin see-through rings that fade when idle. The left stick moves forward and back (sideways strafes, like the gamepad's left stick) and the right stick looks around. Both work at once on a phone and can be dragged with the mouse on desktop. They only appear in Free-roam (not in VR), and the Controls tab has a checkbox to hide them.

versions.label: GS 0.975
changes: The desktop and phone view now shows everything the VR view shows. Both draw up to 100 m, but on desktop that used to be counted from the camera, which sits behind where you stand in VR (4 m by default, up to 50 m zoomed out), so faraway objects visible in VR could disappear. Desktop now counts from where you'd stand in VR. VR itself is unchanged.

versions.label: GS 0.974
changes: Added Merge scenes to the Community tab: pick two Community scenes (with the 🔀 button on each row or the Merge scenes bar), say how to combine them, and the AI blends their gameplay, controls and assets into a new scene.

You can choose where each part comes from (gameplay, controls, assets, environment and lighting, UI) and write a prompt. Images and other large assets are carried over exactly without being sent to the AI.

The merge never changes either original. The new scene credits both parents, keeps their history, works with Code tab hot reload, and can be refined by chatting and then published or shared like any other scene.

versions.label: GS 0.973
changes: Added a Share tab with a link to the current scene (the same Community share and View-only link) and 3D model export to GLB, glTF, FBX, OBJ and Blender. GLB, glTF and Blender keep the scene's lights. The same buttons are in the VR Scenes panel.
The code window in VR no longer lags: the headset copy of the menu only repaints when something changes (about 9 ms instead of 76 ms per repaint).
VR windows can stay Fixed or Follow your headset (Controls → VR windows, or the button in the VR Environment panel).
Code tab Apply now hot-reloads only the blocks you changed and keeps their state (gs.state, gs.onUpdate). Full reset rebuilds the whole scene.
VR controller triggers, mouse clicks and touch now work on p5 and canvas panels.

Scenes now save the chat and info log that made them. When you publish, you can see what will be shared, and secrets are removed. Reopening a scene brings the chat back as history so you can keep going, and 📜 shows or downloads the full log.

Import existing p5.js sketches onto panels by paste, file, zip, folder or URL, including p5 web editor and OpenProcessing links. Each sketch runs in its own sandbox, is saved with the scene, and can be edited in the Code tab.

versions.label: GS 0.972
changes: Added ammo.js physics to the page. It is on by default, and scenes that need gravity or collisions use it.
Added a Dependencies tab listing THREE.js, ammo.js and p5.js, with a toggle for each library.
Added a 2D / 3D choice in the Environment tab: 2D uses p5.js or a blank canvas, 3D uses THREE.js (the default) or plain WebGL. The AI follows your choice.
Added game controller support (Xbox Series X|S and other USB or Bluetooth pads): sticks move and look, triggers zoom, Y switches camera mode, and generated scenes can read the controller.
Added a changelog for every version to this version list.

versions.label: GS 0.971
changes: Added a Controls tab for the desktop and phone camera: Orbit (the default), Free-roam (WASD to move, mouse to look, Q/E up and down, Shift to go faster) and Off.
Orbit now circles the scene origin from the first load.
Turned off panning in Orbit mode.

versions.label: GS 0.970
changes: Added a dock at the bottom of the screen that holds the Enter VR button and the version button, so they no longer overlap.

versions.label: GS 0.969
changes: Added Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT6 Sol and GPT6 Luna to the model dropdown.

versions.label: GS 0.968
changes: Fixed the Community Scenes layout on desktop.

versions.label: GS 0.967
changes: Added the GS version button and version picker.
First numbered build. It includes all earlier work, most recently:
Code editor syntax highlighting, a 360 / HDRI environment option and a desktop WASD fix.
An HTML-in-canvas menu in VR.
GPT6.1 Sol in the model dropdown.
Loading a community scene clears the world first, with a Layer option and no duplicate loads.
The chat window fits on phones, keeps its header inside the visible Safari viewport, and defaults to a see-through panel with a solid border.

note: Newest first. Each entry: { id, label, url, date, changes[] }. url null = this deployment; otherwise a full https URL (Vercel preview, pinned Worker, etc.). changes are shown as the changelog in the version picker.
